claim: The site selects a current installer for macOS, Windows, or Linux.
sandbox: mocked GitHub latest-release API with one real-shaped asset per platform; assert the selected URL

claim: Successful release metadata stays in the browser cache for one hour.
sandbox: seed a cache record just under the one-hour limit and assert no request; set it exactly at the limit and assert a refreshed GitHub API request

claim: The site loads only its own files and public GitHub release metadata, not tracker, analytics, font, or runtime-script services.
sandbox: record every request during a fresh landing-page visit with a mocked release response; assert that the only origins are the product preview and api.github.com

claim: The sample check uses built-in data and saves no demo records.
where: landing demo banner, privacy copy, and README
sandbox: fresh browser context at ?demo=1; reset sample; assert the demo namespace stays empty

claim: The sample check shows covered text and author metadata.
sandbox: fresh browser context at ?demo=1 with built-in sample result

claim: Single-file checking, cleaning, and JSON export are free; Pro batch work is a US$12 one-time offer and remains unavailable until checkout registration is ready.
where: landing facts and pricing, app license panel, README
sandbox: fresh site and app contexts; assert free features, exact price, batch scope, and an explicitly disabled purchase control with the billing-registration status

claim: PDF parsing is local and the parser sandbox cannot open files or network sockets.
where: landing privacy copy, desktop privacy assurances, privacy policy, README
sandbox: forked Linux worker enters the production Landlock/seccomp policy; assert open and socket system calls return permission denied

claim: The app detects covered and invisible text, metadata, annotations, attachments, actions, forms, and layers in at least 95% of the regression corpus.
where: landing checks, app introduction, README, researched success measure
sandbox: 24 committed varied PDF fixtures; assert each expected finding and print detected/total by category

claim: Sanitizing leaves the original bytes unchanged, creates a separate copy, removes detected risky structures, and checks the copy again.
where: landing preview and workflow, app result, README
sandbox: sanitize every risky corpus fixture in memory; compare original hash and bytes, then re-inspect the separate result for a pass

claim: The JSON proof identifies the source and sanitized copy by SHA-256 without exporting a local path.
where: landing preview and file identity, app result, README
sandbox: serialize a report with source and sanitized hashes; assert both identities remain and both local paths are absent

claim: The app rejects a PDF larger than 500 MB before reading it.
sandbox: create a sparse 500 MB plus one byte PDF path; assert TooLarge before file contents are read

claim: On Linux, the PDF worker has a 60-second CPU limit and a 1.5 GB address-space limit.
sandbox: start the production worker command in a fresh process, read its active rlimits after its sandbox starts, and assert the exact CPU and address-space values

claim: The built-in desktop sample works with no external request.
sandbox: fresh desktop UI context with all external requests recorded; load the built-in sample and assert none occur

claim: License checks send only the entered license token.
where: landing privacy copy, desktop license panel, privacy policy
sandbox: fresh desktop UI context with a captured mocked billing request; enter a known token and assert the GET has that token only and no body
